Reports that OpenAI discussed giving the federal government a 5% stake should concern anyone who wants the US to set the pace in AI, says Cato’s @DeHavenTad. Government ownership blurs the line between referee and market participants, creating political risk for developers, customers, and international partners. 
 
“Washington should strengthen US competitiveness through clear, neutral rules—not by taking equity in the companies it regulates.”

The Supreme Court just ruled presidents can fire members of independent agencies at will. That means restructuring the CFPB under a bipartisan board won't shield it from politics. The real fix is Congress writing clear limits on what the agency can do, says Cato’s @SolveigSinglet.

posts.text:
Republicans and Democrats are finding rare common ground: taxing AI. But should they? Cato’s Adam Michel and Daniel Bunn of the Tax Foundation dismantle the three biggest arguments around the idea: showing why the data don’t support the claims that AI is replacing workers, labor is losing out to capital, or the tax code unfairly favors automation.

Listen on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and our website!

Jones Act defenders argue the law ensures a robust US shipbuilding industry. But the data show otherwise. The US ranked 19th in global shipbuilding in 2025 with 0.03% of output.

The Jones Act's bargain is broken, and American consumers and businesses are paying for it, reports Cato’s @cpgrabow.
